8i0fat:258: Traditional Pydantic solved the pain of human-filled forms—usernames too long, emails missing @, phone numbers short by a digit. Error patterns are stable and enumerable, so a single error has actionable value. In the LLM era, the validation target is JSON output. Run the same prompt 100 times: the 1st run might have a field name missing an underscore, the 47th might introduce an undefined field, the 89th might stuff None into a str field—error patterns are drifting and probabilistic. A single error has no directional value; you must look at trend distributions across batches. The original article uses a three-stage factory QC analogy for this migration: "manual item-by-item inspection of finished goods" → "sampling + SPC statistics" → "online monitoring + real-time correction."
